Mentally stronger - In addition to building physical strength, the training with Jason really helps me feel more powerful mentally and has given me a fighting spirit to better deal with the daily stresses and life’s challenging situations. Also, I came to realise that boxing is an excellent way to get to know myself. I started to understand more about how my brain works and reacts which helped me improve mentally in every way, from thinking clearly in intense situations to breathing, balancing and sharpening my reflexes. As you begin learning how to stay balanced in boxing, subconsciously you also begin learning how to balance yourself better in life.

Technically stronger - If you find some other classes do not emphasise technique, every class at STRONGER BOXING is guaranteed to not only make you work hard but also leave you with a greater understanding of the sweet science. Boxing is a lot more strategic than simply throwing random punches and STRONGER BOXING is heavily focused on the technical side. Jason is so thorough in explaining and always shares valuable fight tactics and boxing strategies that will help you become much more intelligent and skillful in order to be a stronger, smarter fighter.

Great training environment for all levels – The people in our Sunday group classes are so friendly and welcoming. I am a big introvert but from day 1, I have never felt intimidated by the group. More importantly the coach adjusts his training to accommodate for all levels, no matter if you are a corporate person who have never thrown a punch or if you are an experienced boxer. Each session is very well thought out and cleverly designed. Jason clearly puts a lot of time and dedication into designing these sessions which are full of variety and lots of fun.

A professional coach that will look after you – Jason is so passionate, patient, and accommodating. Even in the group classes where there are so many trainees, he always pays close attention to each person and never makes them feel left out. He is also extremely knowledgeable on how our bodies work. Most importantly while he motivates me to push myself hard, he also ensures that my technique is always correct to avoid any injuries.

Every person I know is so surprised to see how much I have transformed myself through boxing. All of that is credited to Jason. If I could give you 10 Stars, I would!
Muay Thai was something that my 16 year old son, Josh had discovered and quietly researched on his own in the past two years. He had tried out a few martial art forms in the past but lost interest simply because he was not inspired, he needed more than just step by step learning.
He needed Authenticity and a Kind environment! And our family Moto has always been, ‘If it’s Not Fun or Kind, Don’t do it’!!!

After reading up about some of the coaches inspiring journeys with Muay Thai Camps, Josh was convinced MSP Gym would be the authentic experience that he has been searching for years.

But more than authenticity, kind environment and sound disciplines, Josh also felt a huge sense of respect everyone has for the coaches and vice versa which further encouraged him to sign up as a member.

Josh felt extremely welcomed from the moment he stepped on the mat on his first class few weeks ago. He is enjoying his learning from Mardsing, Wut and Ang, he appreciates their attention to detail and patient guidance to suit his individual needs.

Chantelle, Thank you kindly for speaking to me on the phone with such patience, your kind assistance was part of why I encouraged Josh to have his first visit.

Thank you all for holding a safe and inspiring space for Josh to learn his new found martial art form/sport.
The joy on Josh’s face after each class is enough for us to drive all the way from the Blue Mountains twice a week.

10 Stars to you all!
🌟 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟
With warmth and gratitude,

The marketing is gimmicky and the whole place feels more like a TikTok gym than somewhere you should be paying $66 a week for. For that kind of money, you should be getting structured boxing training, not whatever this is.

Let’s start with the owner, Andrew. He is one of the most arrogant and big-headed people I’ve ever met. It’s his way or the highway, and he acts like nobody understands boxing except him. According to Andrew, his syllabus is the only thing that works and world-class fighters and coaches don’t understand boxing properly because they don’t understand “body mechanics.” Think about that for a second. Fighters like Floyd Mayweather, Canelo Alvarez, Manny Pacquiao, Roberto Durán and countless others have achieved more in boxing than most people could dream of, yet Andrew talks as if he’s cracked the code that everyone else has missed.

His understanding of boxing is apparently so advanced that he doesn’t believe in pad work, ab work, strength and conditioning, or many of the training methods used by boxing gyms all over the world. Instead, the vast majority of what you’ll be doing is shadowboxing and bag work. That’s it. Don’t expect the sort of drills and training methods that are standard at almost every other boxing gym because Andrew believes he knows better than all of them.

There are no real set class times either. You just show up and see what happens. Maybe you’ll spar, maybe you’ll stand around shadowboxing. There are no timers, no structured rounds for drills, and very little organisation. People just go until they’re tired and then stop.

What makes it even harder to take seriously is the constant talk about having the answer to boxing while there is very little evidence of the gym producing active amateur boxers who compete regularly. After completing 27 classes at F45 Oxford Circus, I can honestly say this is one of the best decisions I have ever made. I only wish I had discovered it sooner — I would have started years ago.

The impact on my daily life has been truly life-changing. Years of extended desk work had left me with persistent pain and stiffness, but since joining, my day-to-day tasks feel noticeably easier and that discomfort has significantly reduced. On top of that, my stamina and strength have improved in ways I didn't expect so quickly.

What I love most is the variety — I've attended strength, Pilates, and cardio classes all under one roof. There really is something for every goal and every mood, and the programming keeps things fresh every single session.

The staff and coaches are genuinely the nicest, most inspiring people. A special shoutout to Ally and Sam — they are consistently present, attentive, and always ready to push you in the best way possible. That kind of coaching makes a real difference to your progress and keeps you coming back.

I’m in East London competing in the London Open Veterans Judo Tournament, representing Team USA as a National Champion — and if you know the sport, you know weigh-ins aren’t just a formality… they’re everything. Managing weight before competition is one of the most stressful parts of the process, and having access to an accurate scale can make or break your mindset going into fight day.

I stopped into Diesel Gym London needing a quick check — and what I got was way more than that.

From the moment I walked in, the team was welcoming, professional, and completely dialed in. They had a spot-on digital scale, and without hesitation, they let me use it. No hassle, no attitude — just genuine support for an athlete in the middle of prep.

The facility itself has a serious, high-performance energy — the kind of place where people are there to work, improve, and compete. You can feel it immediately. The coaches and members carry that same mindset: focused, respectful, and driven.

That quick stop took a huge weight off my shoulders (literally and mentally) heading into tomorrow.

Massive shoutout to the Diesel Gym team for stepping up when it counted. If you’re a fighter, competitor, or anyone serious about training in London — this is a spot you want in your corner.

Highly recommend if you’re this part of London ! Thanks Cliff & The Coaches

[{"Name":"Puichi H","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjVBuQ8U3_MBhcSk_7tSufITEeb4BvFwpf8jnv-g4YXbE11Qv-VpSw=s120-c-rp-mo-ba12-br100","Rating":5,"Description":"I first heard of Hiitbeat back in January 2024. I was already a member at another gym and had attended a solo Spin class with Michaela, one of the PTs at Hiitbeat. As soon as my gym membership expired, I attended a couple of classes at Hiitbeat during the summer of 2025 to get a feel for what it was like before committing.

Between May and September 2025, I went to various classes at Hiitbeat, and finally made the decision in January 2026 to get locked-in and take part in the six-week transformation programme, which was a complete game changer for me. It was easily one of the best decisions I’ve ever made! The six weeks helped me stay consistent, accountable and motivated. Attending four 6am classes every week was brutal, but it’s amazing how quickly you adapt when your mind and body are aligned and committed to improving your health and fitness goal.

I’ve left it quite a while to write this review because I wanted to do this place, the structure, the variety of class types, and the quality and calibre of the coaches justice. I can honestly say there’s no other gym, no coaches, and no community that has ever pushed me as much as the people here.

I go to the Hiitbeat in Waltham Abbey, and they also have a studio in Chingford. Both gyms have amazing equipments and facilities to support you with your goals.

I’ve now been a solid member since January 2026, and in the last four months I’ve discovered my love for CrossFit-style training. I’ve even purchased my first Myzone belt, which shows how seriously I’m taking it.
I’m also partnering with Mark, one of the coaches, to take part in my first ATHX competition in August alongside a lot of the Hiitbeat family. It still hasn’t quite sunk in. Mark is one of the most supportive and encouraging coaches there is. He’s a bit crazy and really puts us through our paces, but he’s a massive inspiration and just fab!

I genuinely love all the coaches and all the classes. I try to attend as many as I can, but with work it’s mostly early mornings, late evenings and weekends.

If I miss a Saturday, I get real FOMO...

The first thing that hits you is the atmosphere. It’s authentic, focused, and full of positive energy without any ego or intimidation. The space is clean, well-maintained, and filled with real boxing equipment — heavy bags, speed bags, gloves, pads, and everything you need for a proper session. You immediately get the sense that this is a place where people come to work hard and improve.

But what really sets Kingsway Boxing Club apart is the coaching team. The trainers are incredible — knowledgeable, patient, passionate, and real professionals. They know how to break things down for beginners while still pushing more advanced boxers to refine technique and build endurance. They take the time to correct your form, teach you proper footwork, and motivate you without ever making you feel overwhelmed. Their energy is contagious, and it’s clear they love what they do.

The classes are well-structured, engaging, and intense in the best way. You get a mix of technique, conditioning, bag work, pad work, and drills that leave you feeling stronger each time. Whether you’re there for fitness, skill development, or stress relief, every session feels worthwhile. You always walk out feeling accomplished — tired, sweaty, but proud.

The community at Kingsway Boxing Club is another highlight. Members are friendly, supportive, and diverse. You see people of all levels and all ages coming together to train, laugh, and push themselves. It feels like a local family gym rather than a corporate chain — personal, genuine, and motivating.

From a value standpoint, it’s fantastic. You really feel like you’re getting expert coaching and a premium experience. The staff are welcoming, check-ins are easy, and everyone treats you with respect and positivity.

Overall, Kingsway Boxing Club is a top-tier boxing gym — well-run, inspiring, professionally coached, and filled with great energy. Whether you’re looking to get in shape, learn real boxing technique, or join a supportive community, this place delivers. [{"Name":"Ted Chen","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjXx4SHAAe893EnVSjNkJKItJfJOwYcb-OXfgEM7F3fc88rl8G_9=s120-c-rp-mo-ba12-br100","Rating":5,"Description":"The PIT Personal Training completely changed my perception of what a gym should be. As someone who had never trained at a gym before, I couldn't have asked for a better introduction to strength training. The space is thoughtfully designed and fully equipped with an impressive range of specialized equipment that you don't often find in commercial gyms. Every piece of equipment feels intentionally selected, creating an environment that's ideal for both beginners and experienced lifters alike.

What truly sets The PIT apart, however, is its people. Every trainer I've interacted with has been welcoming, professional, and genuinely passionate about helping clients succeed. There's a strong sense of community here that makes every session something to look forward to.

My trainer, Miles, deserves special recognition. At just 21 years old, he has a level of knowledge, technical precision, and coaching maturity that genuinely surprised me. His understanding of biomechanics, exercise selection, programming, and progression rivals—and in many cases surpasses—that of trainers with many more years of experience.

His programs are exactly how strength training should be: structured, progressive, sustainable, and individualized. Every session has a clear purpose. The progression is challenging enough to drive results while remaining manageable, avoiding the common trap of excessive fatigue or random "beat-you-up" workouts. It's intelligent coaching backed by solid reasoning.

And yes, I have to say it: if your trainer's name is Miles, you should fully expect to go the extra mile... or rather, the extra Miles. 😄 He has an uncanny ability to know when to push you harder and when to hold you back, striking the perfect balance between motivation and long-term progress.

Beyond the gym floor, Miles is simply great company. He's personable, humble, and remarkably wise beyond his years. Conversations between sets can effortlessly move from training science and nutrition to investing, chess, technology, travel, and a surprising range of intellectually engaging topics. It's rare to find someone who can coach your body while also keeping your mind engaged throughout the session.

If you're looking for a boutique gym that combines outstanding facilities, evidence-based coaching, a welcoming atmosphere, and trainers who genuinely care about your long-term success, The PIT Personal Training is an easy five-star recommendation. And if you're fortunate enough to train with Miles, you'll quickly understand why going the extra Miles is one of the best investments you can make in your health.","Images":["https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/grass-cs/ACvplmPdeoo4i11ztocUC0C7e_8iYuShf5iGiHr6yzdyMS1k-CfYsms2HzH0f7tcrn44bEefYvnDdrmCLyu0d2mbieoJEe-0VM3pdkGWM9FgGiwMrrko62EbPBMIzNV_d3YZlRZVEDNFN0Mmaec=k-no","https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/grass-cs/ACvplmPveAZnw2pdi11nVtPoq5PUZHCeVob9b8Y937l3khzrWrSMUvu_VuM-_MslGcSJEkk-fM3NM7uKW7O0trm0bdQPhruGa1daDxEpLvK1NYUwSeERNR4f_N5V2TM71BV6cSKW7ZShrv0O_-YO=k-no","https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/grass-cs/ACvplmN6QMRiarEusjHYFzAVISgOC0IhitQuyZgWfPyMxGt-ZqF9RK-dglkaIZ5ck-UvIS4xl1gOMHT5FXSdrHZ0wOYaM94Gmrqtx5MUQRrWm_Sw6zH0rKhEVjoXZkTRjoiv7xlDIRHpyREG2s2N=k-no"],"When":"Edited a month ago","review_id":"Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2pWMWFWTkVhVFJtZDBVNU0ySkhRM1pFYnpoeFlVRRAB","source":"Google","rating_scale":5,"rating_float":5,"author_url":"https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/106959484851880522014/reviews?hl=en-GB","posted_at_unix_micros":1785294293732374,"updated_at_unix_micros":1785546140141876,"language":"en","translated_lang":"","text_original":"The PIT Personal Training completely changed my perception of what a gym should be. Friendly members, encouraging coaches - shoutout to Cheryl and Emman and previously Gifford, Wan Jing and Ian - and athletes and a wonderful place to continue your fitness journey. No matter where you are on the fitness spectrum, there's always something for everyone. Classes available include Crossfit / functional fitness, Olympic lifting, strength, Strongman and gymnastics.  There's also open gym available for people who want to work out on their own.

The current gym is based in an old tennis court, and can sometimes get quite wet if it rains. I genuinely appreciate the effort that Prof Amirul & Coach Daryl put into helping members improve. Unfortunately, my overall experience deteriorated over time due to several recurring issues.

One of the biggest frustrations was the frequent class cancellations, often with very short notice or at times little to no notice at all. Cancellations felt normalised with no replacement coaches at times and as a paying member, it became difficult to plan training consistently when classes could be cancelled at the last minute. Most of us felt shortchanged.

Another concern was the cleanliness and maintenance of the facility. Hygiene standards were not always up to expectations and there were occasions where cockroaches were spotted within the gym premises. This was concerning, especially in a martial arts gym utilising the mats 100% of the time for a high contact sport like jiu jitsu.

What disappointed me most was that these were not isolated incidents. The issues persisted over an extended period and despite feedback from members, there appeared to be little meaningful effort to address or improve them over the past months. As a result, I have since decided to terminate my membership and unfortunately the coaches and community I stayed for have also decided to move on to other opportunities.

Neuefit had strong community and coaches at that time and I’m grateful for the experiences, time spent and friends made but management, operational reliability, communication and facility upkeep need significant improvement.

Providing a clean, professional and dependable training environment should always be priority.

Unfortunately, the move to Raffles Place at the beginning of 2026 marked a significant decline in the overall experience.

The previous Kallang Wave Mall facility was outstanding; great vibes, spacious, better equipped, and offered a far more comfortable training environment. The new space is now half the size, depressing and dirty.

Small gym
- Chaotic and overstimulating atmosphere with Muay Thai, HIIT and BJJ classes all running concurrently in a small space
- Limited space to roll safely without the risk of bumping into people, stairs, or the reception counter

Feedback was often met with excuses or promises that never seemed to materialize
- Changing rooms: As a female member, this was my main concern. I’ve raised that the changing areas were separated only by curtains, that they could be easily blown open by the air-conditioning, and that anyone could pull them open without knowing there’s someone inside. Many members also suggested replacing them with proper doors to provide privacy and security. This was raised in January,  and curtains were changed to doors only in June, after many members had already become frustrated. It is quite telling when members feel more comfortable changing and using mall’s toilets before coming to the gym.

Hygiene standards were an ongoing issue
- The shower areas frequently smelled of pee
- Cockroaches seen at changing area, water cooler area, mats) on several occasions
- After classes, our white gis would often turn grey. (We were told that a deep clean would be carried out, but this never happened)

Communication between management and members was often poor. Operational staff were not particularly effective in their roles
- Last minute class cancellations
- Important changes, such as the departure of key coaches and the gym’s relocation, were often communicated very late, and we usually hear about such information via word of mouth from other members instead of from the gym directly
- Members had to personally ask staff to verify our membership validity periods, as they were incorrect due to gym relocation extensions or injury breaks etc. These were never updated proactively for the rest of the members though several of us has already asked them to. Hence, to date, members who have never realised / asked would still have been shortchanged

Sadly, there used to be a fantastic community and a strong team of coaches that made the place special. Members genuinely wanted to see the gym flourish, do well, and grow its community. We’ve tried giving feedback and gave them time to make changes, yet things still remained unchanged. Eventually, people simply gave up. Now that the best coaches and many of the long-time members have left, I have unfortunately decided to leave as well.

I hope, moving forward, the management will be more receptive to member’s feedback, rather than assuming overall satisfaction with their current efforts, when that is not reflected in members’ private conversations at all.

However, after attending a trial, my impression changed completely.

The first shock was discovering that the competition BJJ class was gone. Even during what should have been a busy after-work period, attendance was extremely low. The atmosphere felt empty and stagnant rather than thriving.

I was also unimpressed by the coaching. During demonstrations, coaches were losing basic gi grips, which immediately made me question the quality of the instruction. The biggest disappointment was the culture. The welcoming community I thought I was joining simply did not exist. The front desk staff came across as cliquey and unwelcoming. Nobody showed me around the gym or made any effort to help me settle in. Instead, staff seemed more interested in chatting amongst themselves, and I even overheard them openly speaking negatively about members, which was incredibly unprofessional.

To make matters worse, after class I saw a staff member openly taking a nap. That pretty much summed up the overall impression of the gym: poor professionalism, poor management, and a complete lack of care.

At this point, I am not surprised that members have left. The BJJ team appears to have significantly downsized compared to what the gym previously posted and bragged about on social media. The coaches who were prominently featured in those posts also seem to no longer be there. Instead, the gym is left with coaches who, based on what I observed during my trial, did not inspire much confidence in their technical ability. The facility is small, the management feels thoughtless, the culture is disappointing, and the reality of the gym falls far short of the image it tries to project online.

I have had 7 years of MT/ Boxing experience before Blessed and I have to say my striking skills have improved tremendously since I joined which was only a few months since last Sep. The gym is also generally welcoming towards testing cross train skill sets in sparring (e.g. Sanda, Judo, wrestling) with a heavy caveat of course that this is done safely and skilfully and within the prevailing sparring ruleset (MT, Boxing or BJJ) and not in a spazzy manner from some technique picked up on YouTube that is not at least adequately drilled.

Never had a bad or boring class so far but I would like to shout out to the following coaches (other coaches are awesome too ♥️♥️)

1) Amir Gani - gym owner and very experienced. Welcoming attitude and willing to add value to members by giving specific guidance to upgrade their skills. For example, I am more of an in pocket fighter susceptible to kiting. He specifically had a class to teach anti kiting long range techniques to debug my flawed software.
2) Bryan Tee(p) - former ONE fighter and makes me feel like a noob from day one till date. I have significantly increased my skill repertoire under him (combinations, clinching, takedowns) and improved my execution sharpness. It is very telling that he can consistently sweep me multiple times in a sparring round despite me being 87 kg and him being 50+kg, and also that I am a judoka.
3) Jason Wu - BJJ instructor previously under 10 planet system and ex Wushu athlete. Delivers anti blue belt techniques to me and is able to also informally coach me on my other areas of interest e.g. Chinese style shuaijiao, MMA, trad Chinese martial arts, weapons fighting). Definition of a hidden gem
4) Ray - didn't train with him much but enjoyed the few classes that he did as he breaks things down specifically and well so that it is not just a fitness class but also technical. Enjoy sparring with him and shame he has to start NS now.
5) MD Sujimi "Jimmy" - very professional and fun coach who adds value to training of beginners and intermediate students. Strong recommendation to join his class if you are just starting to learn Muay Thai and want a coach with a "easy" personality to make it less intimidating. Also no slouch in technique - I saw him punch the bag on multiple occasions (during demonstration) bareknuckle - this requires elite technique.
6) Furqan Faizal - Singapore rep for SEA games MMA and a super anal coach in terms of correcting your bad habits. Very mature beyond his years and 20 min of MMA sparring session with him exhausts me out more than 4 hours of back to back classes (which is expected sparring with a pro)
7) Lee Yijun - doesn't get enough credit for her coaching maybe because it is overshadowed by her good work being the gym's "front desk" but I do enjoy her boxing class which focuses on basics and footwork application. In my limited opinion, getting your jab cross hook, head movement, and footwork right gets you out of the "newbie" bracket the fastest

The biggest difference is the coaching style. Our previous gym was very disciplinary in approach, which over time became demoralising for both my son and me. I want to be fair here and say that some people genuinely thrive under that kind of strict coaching, and I respect that. It just wasn’t right for us. At Spartans Springleaf, Coaches Zak (Head Coach), Danish, and Khlifi have made boxing enjoyable again. For the first time in a long while, my son and I are actually looking forward to training. And the fun comes with real credibility — these are highly qualified coaches and ex-national boxers, so you’re getting proper technique and genuine expertise alongside all the encouragement.

A special mention has to go to Head Coach Zak. His patience really stands out, and even on a bad training day he never makes you feel lousy or judged. On top of that, he has a real gift for bringing out the fun in boxing. That combination is exactly what my son and I needed, and it’s a big part of why we look forward to every session. The rest of the coaches are fantastic too.

The facilities are also a clear step up. Spartans Springleaf is more updated, air-conditioned, and you can tell they put real effort into hygiene. Our old gym was naturally ventilated, but the upkeep didn’t keep pace - spoilt fans weren’t repaired or replaced promptly, and the sponge flooring stayed tattered and torn for the entire 1.5 years we were there without ever being replaced.

One note for anyone comparing gyms in the north by their ratings: review count doesn’t tell the whole story. Our previous gym actively asked members to leave Google reviews, whereas Spartans Springleaf simply lets the coaching speak for itself. They may have fewer reviews than others nearby, but in our experience they’re the better gym by a clear margin.

Immediately, I pledged my loyalty to RTF and Master Chan and signed a package.

What I really like that spurs my almost compulsive decision?

1.  The price is really affordable. I was doing Muay Thai at a franchise gym, and it costs me $70/session on top of the monthly membership fee of $145. So when Master Chan offered me the package I couldn't refuse.

2. The First In - First Out training style. You reach, you skip, you HIIT, and then padworks with the trainers. Not your turn yet? Go practise moves on those sandbags. I've never tried other gyms so I can't compare training style but this style works for me.

3. The camaraderie among the students. Students who goes there really just wants to have fun and keep fit at the same time. There's no competition and each of us genuinely wants to help each other improve. Some students are now trainers as well. You progress at your own speed.

4. The open air gym. It's so old school, I like. Open air training is better for muay thai. You don't really want your sweats to get chilled by aircon. Oh, they have ceiling fans but it's not operational during training. Warnings given in advance.

The Khan levels was introduced a few years after I joined them. They'll prep you before the exams so you'll know what to expect. And when you reach Khan 3 and 4, you will be able to join the muay thai competition to fight with the students in Thailand's affiliated gym, or the International Muay Thai Festival fights with other overseas competitors. Very exciting events during August! (pre-covid)

user_reviews:
[{"Name":"g","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocKlVgTmCydY3VT_e4N4AT0WPPURP3KK9E0e6dWsLiRPGRYgTQ=s120-c-rp-mo-ba12-br100","Rating":1,"Description":"Went for a trial and was thoroughly disappointed by how the situation was handled.

tldr gave my budget 💲and they said it fit my budget but realised after my trial that it didnt 🥹, messy handling of communication 📱😥 and got blamed when giving feedback about precautions ⚠️😓

1. Informed them about my budget and checked if they had plans that fit. They had 0 disclosure about the price scheme so I was sure they had both monthly pricing and lesson packages like I've seen when checking with other martial arts centres.

However, to my shock, they informed me they only had monthly classes and surprise! It did not fit my budget, it would be great if I was informed of this earlier. But I was asked to pay 30 and go for the trial just to know about the cost. I admit I took the risk even though I didn't know what type of pricing they had, and I guess it was my fault trusting that they could fit my budget 😅

Tried to talk over whatsapp about it but the lack of sympathy is quite astonishing to be honest 😅

2. Was told that I would be introduced to the prices after the trial and if I didn't sign up on the spot, there would be no waiver. However, I checked with the trainer after the trial that day and she told me I would be contacted through whatsapp. My trial ended at 12pm, and I waited till 3.30pm without any message from them before I contacted them myself. After which I was left there for about 4 hours before I was introduced to the price at night when I was already asleep.

I understand they may be busy, but telling me there was only waiver if I signed up on the spot/ on the day itself and then taking so long to reply really gave me a lot of anxiety. I felt like my time wasn't appreciated at all and I was chasing them for a reply. Didn't sign up after this harrowing experience, so I didn't know if they would've given me the waiver anyway despite what they said.

3. I had rings on my right hand before starting the class and pardon my folly and lack of basic knowledge, but I wasn't aware that it was very important to remove all the jewelry before wearing the boxing gloves. Sometimes people may forget to remove them too, even if it is basic knowledge. The instructor didn't inform me of any precautions and there were no signages in the space, so I didn't remove my rings. During the session, I asked if it was normal if my fingers hurt while punching and the trainer said it might have been because I didn't have my gloves on. Removed my gloves at the end of the class, saw my ring, and realised it might have been the problem. A short search online made me realise it posed a risk for significant injury!

I gave some feedback over whatsapp because I hoped more precautions would be taken so others wouldn't be at risk of injury, but lo and behold, I was blamed for it 😅😅

Thanks for reading this lengthy review and I really hope the owner takes these feedback into account. From the start, Coach Choco, who attended to us at the counter, sarcastically asked why I bought my daughter Muay Thai shorts,  “for fashion?” I brushed it off as I was focused on making her first class a positive experience. I later heard across the window that the comment had been joked about among themselves, which made it even more inappropriate. One of the other people in the gym even questioned her about what she had said to me, to which she responded proudly, “What? It's true what.”

Barely three minutes into the class, Coach Choco came out and told me, “She can’t skip leh, Not suitable for her.” My daughter is only 4 years old and was genuinely trying her best to learn how to skip using an adult-sized skipping rope.

So no room at all for improvement?

Halfway through the class, my daughter needed to use the washroom. When she returned, there was little to no encouragement or guidance given to her. She eventually became upset, broke down and left the class.

After the class, I approached Coach Choco hoping for a quick debrief on what my daughter could work on and with the intention of returning the following week. Instead, I was simply told, “Not ready — wait another 6 months.”

Again, no room at all for improvement.

I understand that not every child may be suitable for every class, but the way this was handled was disappointing and lacked the patience, encouragement and professionalism I would expect when dealing with a 4-year-old attending her very first trial.
